title: Lightship: 90-minute SDK Rapid Probe & Integration Manifest
content:
Context:
A compact, repeatable 90-minute lab designed for engineers evaluating Redwood SDK integration surface area and first-touch reliability signals. The intention is not to be a full onboarding but a targeted probe to validate: streaming stability, token accounting, telemetry semantics, local dev ergonomics, and common failure modes (timeouts, retries, kv cache warmup).

Audience:
- Backend and full-stack engineers doing initial SDK integration
- Solutions engineers running customer proof-of-concepts
- Developer-experience squad members validating SDK changes against real flows

Success criteria (observable within the session):
1) Sample app can successfully stream a 500-token assistant response to the UI without rebuffering or duplicated tokens.
2) Token accounting visible in SDK telemetry matches server-side token delta within 2%.
3) Retry/backoff path exercised: app recovers from a simulated 503 with no more than one visible error to end-user.
4) Local dev loop (mock + live switch) completes under 60s for cold start.

Prerequisites (10 min):
- Attendee has Node 18+ or Python 3.11 installed
- Clone lightweight probe repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-lightship-probe
- API key (test scope) set in env: REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Docker available for optional local runtime

Lab flow (60 min):
1) Warmup (10 min)
   - Start the sample UI (next.js minimal) and backend shim (express/fastapi).
   - Run the simple text generation flow against sandbox model. Observe streaming enabled by default.
   - Confirm baseline telemetry appears in local logs.

2) Streaming stability deep-dive (15 min)
   - Trigger a long-form generation (target 400–700 tokens).
   - Introduce artificial network jitter using 'tc' or the built-in network throttler script.
   - Verify: client displays tokens incrementally, order preserved, no token truncation.
   - Notes: if rebuffering occurs, capture browser devtools HAR and SDK debug log; file an issue template.

3) Token accounting & cost sanity (10 min)
   - Call the tokens endpoint (probe helper) to estimate tokens for prompt+response, then make a live request.
   - Compare SDK-reported token usage (telemetry event) against platform invoices snapshot for the session.
   - Acceptable drift: <=2%; if >2% then flag quantization/encoding mismatch.

4) Failure modes & graceful degradation (10 min)
   - Simulate 503 and 429 from backend via a toggle.
   - Validate SDK exponential backoff, circuit break triggers after N failures, and the app falls back to cached summary.
   - Validate surfaced error messages include request_id and short remediation hints.

5) Telemetry and tracing validation (10 min)
   - Confirm per-request spans include model_name, route, cost_estimate, and kv_cache_status.
   - Inject a synthetic bad prompt that triggers eval regression guard and ensure an alerting event is emitted to the local sink.

Checklist for the facilitator (pre-run):
- Ensure probe repo is at tag v1.0-lightship
- Seed a small prompt set for reproducible outputs (prompts/seed_prompts.json)
- Prepare a short slide with objectives and success criteria
- Prepare mock billing snapshot to compare token counts

Post-run artifacts to collect (if running as POC):
- HAR + SDK debug logs (zip)
- Telemetry export for 30 minutes after run (JSONL)
- Short incident note if retry/circuit-breaker behavior observed

Common pitfalls & mitigation notes:
- "Streaming stops mid-sentence": usually due to premature connection close; confirm keepalive/timeout and increase socket read timeout in shim.
- "Token mismatch large": check for UTF-8 vs UTF-16 encoding differences in client tooling and run tokenizer locally.
- "Backoff too aggressive for interactive apps": adjust SDK policy to prefer jittered linear backoff for user-facing endpoints.

Next steps and probes to escalate into tickets:
- Measurement: Add an automated assertion in e2e tests that verifies streaming order under 5 simulated network conditions (ticket: SDK-2148).
- Telemetry: Add token-precision field to per-request metrics to reduce ambiguity in billing reconciliation (ticket: SDK-2150).
- DX: Create a tiny public gist with minimal reproduction for each common failure mode.

Runbook snippets (cheat answers for facilitators):
- How to quickly get a streaming HAR: open chrome://net-export, start capture before re-running flow, reproduce, stop and export.
- How to correlate SDK logs with server trace: use request_id header; server traces include same id in trace metadata.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Should the probe include a short quantized model path to test client-side footprint? (pending perf team input)
- Consider a variant of the probe that uses the Dedicated routing policy to validate fallbacks across capacity tiers.

Appendix: quick commands
- Clone: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-lightship-probe.git
- Start backend (node): REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxx npm run dev:backend
- Start UI: npm run dev:ui
- Network jitter helper: scripts/network_throttle.sh 200ms 50ms
- Collect logs: scripts/collect_run_artifacts.sh > run_artifacts_$(date +%s).zip

Contact for follow-up: Maya Thompson (maya@redwood.com) - add 'lightship-probe' tag on Slack for ad-hoc assistance.
